st.headline: Bond market is a buy right now, J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s fixed income head says
st.teaser: The bond market has rebounded following a sell-off in October and September.
fullText: SINGAPORE – There is a “generational amount of yield” in bond markets and it is time to buy debt, with a return of as much as 8% on offer in the US over the next the year, Bob Michele, J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s head of global fixed income, said on Oct 27 .
The bond market has rebounded following a sell-off in October and September , especially in developed-market sovereign debt.
“We expect both the Fed funds rate and the Treasury curve to converge (around 4.5%),” Michele told reporters in Singapore.
“Generally at the end of a hiking cycle the yield curve is flat... so there’s plenty of room for yields to run from where they are.”
Carry and price appreciation are likely to deliver a return in the US market of 7% to 8% over the next 12 months, he added.
US 10-year yields were around 4.99% on Oct 27 having spent much of the past few weeks above 5%.
Investors expect the Fed funds rate window to stay at 3.75% to 4% when the Federal Reserve announces its interest rate decision on Oct 28 .

“There is yield all over the place,” said Michele. “When we looked at the Treasury curve a few weeks ago when it first went above 5%, to us the buy signal was real yield in the US that got to 3%. The last time we saw that was 2002. So at close to 25 years, that’s a buying opportunity.”
Japan, Australia, investment-grade credit and emerging market sovereign debt are among the stronger picks, he said.

“Everyone senses there’s a generational amount of yield in bond markets,” he said. “It’s pretty clear with the global capex cycle out there, recession is a very low probability. That means every back-up in credit spread (you) should buy.”
The “tail risk,” he said, was the Fed needing to hike much further than 4.5% to contain inflation. REUTERS

cna.headline: China's industrial profit growth picks up amid deepening economic divergence
cna.teaser: China's industrial profit growth picks up amid deepening economic divergence
fullText: BEIJING: China's industrial profits grew at a faster pace in September, though a deepening divergence across the economy weighed on business earnings.

Profits at industrial firms rose 14.4 per cent from a year earlier last month, quickening from a 4.2 per cent increase in August, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed on Tuesday (Oct 27). Profits were up 15.5 per in the first nine months of this year, largely unchanged from the 15.7 per cent increase in the January-August period.

The sectoral divide remained pronounced, with profits in the computer, communication and other electronic equipment manufacturing category more than doubling over the nine-month period, whereas profits in the furniture manufacturing sector fell by more than half, making it one of the worst performers.

Also casting a shadow over the sustainability of profit growth, export-oriented firms are bracing for greater uncertainty as expanding trade surpluses stoke tensions with trading partners, particularly Europe.
"This suggests that domestic and external demand generated by the development of the AI supply chain has become a key force supporting industrial profits," he said.
"Barring a major reversal in the global AI investment boom, industrial profits are expected to continue growing at a rapid pace."

A stronger-than-expected 4.5 per cent expansion in third-quarter GDP put China within reach of its annual growth target of 4.5 per cent to 5.0 per cent, but disparities across different parts of the economy suggest the recovery remains unbalanced, with persistent weakness in some sectors continuing to erode corporate profitability.

That pressure has become increasingly visible at the company level. Net profit growth at the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker, CATL, slowed sharply in the past quarter, as intense competition in the EV battery market squeezed margins at a time when China's auto sales were in a downturn.

China will continue to leverage macroeconomic policies to support growth, expand domestic demand and optimize supply, said NBS statistician Yu Weining, underscoring a push to replace traditional growth drivers with new ones.
Industrial profit figures cover firms with yearly revenue of at least 20 million yuan (US$3.0 million) from main operations.

mom.headline: Tripartite Workgroup Recommends Six Measures to Build Age-Friendly Jobs and Multi-Generational Workplaces
